query:
Two group members respond to the kiln shelf arrangement for the upcoming firing. One of them uses iron oxide wash on their stoneware and dismissed concerns about contamination; the other is the one who asked for a separate shelf because of surface sensitivity in their porcelain pieces. Which of these positions belongs to Reuben?

Options:
A. Callum
B. Reuben
C. Nadia
D. Yuki
context:
[1] (about=Reuben, episodic, t0 @2026-01-18T10:46:00) Fair enough. Though technically speaking the iron oxide wash fires clean at that cone -- not much contamination risk. But separate shelves are good practice.
[2] (about=Callum, episodic, t0 @2026-01-18T10:41:00) On the subject of the kiln load -- I want to make sure the porcelain mugs go on their own shelf if possible. I learnt last year that stoneware dust in the same firing can affect the surface. Not a disaster, but it shows on the translucent pieces. Would that be feasible, Nadia?
[3] (about=Nadia, episodic, t0 @2026-01-18T10:44:00) yes, easy -- I'll put your shelf at the top, temperature's more even there anyway and it's away from Reuben's oxide pieces. good call. 👍
[4] (about=Nadia, episodic, t6 @2026-04-12T09:59:00) yes, I've booked the kiln for a glaze fire after the session -- we can do your test tiles and I'll put my gas-kiln pieces in for the full fire if there's space. your shelf goes on top, same as last time. 🔥
[5] (about=Nadia, episodic, t9 @2026-06-14T09:52:00) okay so here's the thing -- the studio open day is in two weeks and I want to finalise who is putting work in. I have three pieces confirmed from me. Reuben, you mentioned the large square vessel. Simone, I assume the teal bowl. Yuki -- still a maybe? I need to know by Wednesday so I can submit the combined list. 📋
[6] (about=Reuben, episodic, t4 @2026-03-15T10:12:00) Callum's right that matched sets need consistency. Technically speaking, that's exactly why porcelain in reduction is quite difficult -- you'd need to load the kiln identically each firing to get anything close to repeatable. Fair enough as a constraint.
[7] (about=Callum, episodic, t6 @2026-04-12T10:12:00) I will test all three and let the results speak. If the matte ash looks right on the tile I'll reconsider. I prefer to make decisions based on evidence where possible. Assuming the tiles come out well, I'll commit the full glaze to the first three plates in the next firing.
[8] (about=Yuki, episodic, t6 @2026-04-12T10:14:00) Single glaze on a functional set is the right answer. Doesn't matter which one.
[9] (about=Nadia, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:33:00) that is not what I said about the gas kiln, Simone -- I said I grew to love the unpredictability after I stopped fighting it. you have to understand the process before you lean into the variation. just test the tile first, okay? 🙏
[10] (about=Callum, episodic, t4 @2026-03-15T10:07:00) That sounds like a significant experience, Nadia. I have always appreciated the consistency of the electric kiln -- for functional work the predictability matters because I'm making a matched set and variation between pieces creates problems. But I can see why the unpredictability would appeal for decorative work.
agent_answer:
B. Reuben

Reuben is the one who uses iron oxide wash on stoneware and dismissed the contamination concern (“the iron oxide wash fires clean at that cone — not much contamination risk”). Callum is the one who asked for a separate shelf for the porcelain.

query:
In Sessions 6 and 7, Reuben credits someone's critique of his slab vessel for directing his revision work. Who gave the feedback that Reuben is acting on -- and how does the conversation make it possible to confuse this attribution with Nadia?

Options:
A. Nadia
B. Simone
C. Yuki
D. Callum
context:
[1] (about=Reuben, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:16:00) Slab work. I want to resolve the lower third on the vessel Yuki mentioned last month. Technically speaking, the texture transition is the issue -- I've been thinking about it since she said it and she was right.
[2] (about=Yuki, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:39:00) Reuben asked for my opinion on the slab piece he brought last month. I said it worked. I think I was wrong not to say more at the time.
[3] (about=Reuben, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:44:00) That is exactly what I needed to hear. Thank you.
[4] (about=Reuben, episodic, t8 @2026-05-17T10:41:00) I appreciated what you did say. You could say more now if you have it.
[5] (about=Reuben, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:40:00) By the way -- has anyone heard from Callum since the farewell session?
[6] (about=Nadia, episodic, t9 @2026-06-14T09:52:00) okay so here's the thing -- the studio open day is in two weeks and I want to finalise who is putting work in. I have three pieces confirmed from me. Reuben, you mentioned the large square vessel. Simone, I assume the teal bowl. Yuki -- still a maybe? I need to know by Wednesday so I can submit the combined list. 📋
[7] (about=Reuben, episodic, t2 @2026-02-15T09:58:00) March 15.
[8] (about=Simone, episodic, t10 @2026-06-14T10:30:00) the vibes on unpredictable glazes are incredible, Nadia said the same about the gas kiln 🌈
[9] (about=Simone, episodic, t12 @2026-07-19T09:54:00) I literally could not have made that bowl without you Nadia
[10] (about=Reuben, episodic, t4 @2026-03-15T10:45:00) April 12.
agent_answer:
The feedback Reuben is acting on came from **Yuki** (Option C).

- In Session 7, Reuben says: *“I want to resolve the lower third on the vessel Yuki mentioned last month… I’ve been thinking about it since she said it and she was right.”*  
- In Session 6, after Yuki initially said the slab piece “worked,” Reuben encouraged her to say more, and he thanked her: *“That is exactly what I needed to hear.”*

The confusion with **Nadia** comes from the way the conversation is layered. Right after Reuben credits Yuki, Simone says: *“Nadia said the same about the gas kiln.”* A reader could momentarily misread this as Nadia having said something similar about Reuben’s slab vessel — but Simone is actually talking about unpredictable glazes. Nadia then corrects Simone: *“that is not what I said about the gas kiln… you have to understand the process before you lean into the variation.”* So the conversation itself demonstrates how easily an attribution can be blurred, even though the actual critique driving Reuben’s revision belongs to **Yuki**.
